params.what_this_is: The rejected PID configuration on 2025-01-01..2026-11-13, read for reference at the owner's request. Read only after P11's test on the same window was recorded (commit b828de0), so it informed nothing there.
params.verdict: unchanged — rejected, and this window agrees with the rejection.
params.configuration: trend 250, integral 120, derivative 10, kp 0.1, ki 0.1, kd 0.0, base 0.5, band 0.10
params.reading: The rule returned +37.3% against +52.0% for the fixed half position it is built around, with a deeper drawdown (-25.9% against -21.1%) and a Sharpe of 0.77 against 1.10. It was worse than doing nothing with half the money on return, on drawdown and on risk-adjusted return at once. It would have cleared the owner's +10% bar, as any long position did.
params.how_it_behaved_in_the_falls: It did what it is designed to do, and that is the problem. In spring 2025 it went from 67% to 96% of the account as the fund fell 34%, and lost 25.9%. In 2026 it had sold down to 13% by the June peak, which is the idea working, and then bought back to 75% on the way down, losing 20.8% of a 39.5% fall. It is holding 79% now, into 79% annualised volatility; the volatility rule is holding 32%.
params.against_the_volatility_rule_on_the_same_: Volatility rule +60.3%, drawdown -21.9%, Sharpe 1.20. PID +37.3%, -25.9%, 0.77. The two differ in one thing: which way they lean when the fund is falling hard.
